title: Final Project — Student Grade Tracker
description: Build a complete, useful program that stores and reports student grades.

sections.content:
Congratulations — you have made it to the final project.

You have learned: variables, data types, input/output, conditionals, loops, functions, lists, debugging, strings, and dictionaries.

Now you will build something real: a student grade tracker that a teacher could actually use.

The program will:
- Let the teacher add students and their scores
- Show all students and scores
- Calculate the class average
- Find the top student
- Let the teacher search for a student by name

This uses everything you have learned.

sections.explanation: The core data structure is a dictionary where each key is a student name and each value is a list of their scores. Functions keep the code organised.
show_all() loops through all students and prints a formatted table. show_top_student() finds the highest average using the same pattern as finding the largest number in a list.
The main menu loop ties everything together. .title() formats the name so 'aung aung' becomes 'Aung Aung'. {avg:.1f} formats the number to one decimal place.

sections.question: In the grade tracker, why do we store scores as a list (students[name] = []) instead of a single number?
options: So a student can have multiple scores (e.g. for different tests)
It is just a style choice
sections.explanation: A list lets you store multiple scores for the same student — perfect for tracking several tests. A single number would get overwritten each time you added a new score.

sections.prompt: Build the complete grade tracker. Then add one more feature: a function that shows the class average across all students.
sections.hint: For class average: collect all scores from all students into one list, then calculate the average of that combined list.
